topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Their Limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional non-targeted treatment modalities and the systemic toxicity and drug resistance mechanisms that restrict their clinical effectiveness.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Tumor Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that selectively target tumors by exploiting their intrinsic physiological vulnerabilities and genetic defects.

topics.label: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapies designed to inhibit hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and explore the molecular mechanisms through which cancer cells develop resistance or addiction to these agents.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Cancer Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that use engineered monoclonal antibodies to target tumor surface antigens and deliver cytotoxic effects.

topics.label: Immune Surveillance and Checkpoint Blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural immune surveillance against cancer and the clinical application of checkpoint inhibitors that release T-cell inhibition against tumor neoantigens.

topics.label: Engineered T-Cell Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss synthetic immunotherapeutic approaches that physically recruit or genetically reprogram T cells to recognize and destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Clinical Realities, Progress, and Future Outlook of Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on the overall trajectory of oncology by evaluating long-term clinical outcomes against ongoing biological challenges and emerging ethical questions.
